utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, please continue with your examination of Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We will continue where we left off yesterday, and I have a question and then we can move on to another topic regarding the civil defence. First of all, were members of the civil defence armed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with the Law on Defence, they had side-arms for the purpose of their self-defense and self protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have Exhibit 5D300 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me ask you and then we will comment. Who was in charge of arming the members of the civil defence, and you may comment on paragraph 1 in this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that in accordance with the Law on Defence, the organ in charge of organizing, equipping, arming, engaging, and commanding the forces of the civil defence and the civilian protection was the Federal Ministry of Defence of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. We have in front of us a document, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, the federal defence ministry, the district organ in the Republic of Serbia, the Pristina defence administration, as far as I can see that would be the 21st of May, 1998, a task was issued, an order was issued, to the departments and sections for defence. It was addressed personally to chiefs of departments of those regional organs on the implementation of measures for the security and protection of the population, and now I would like to ask the Trial Chamber whether I should just read what it says here or explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Lazarevic, you should listen carefully to the questions and just deal with the point raised. You could have answered that much more briefly, and we can follow the point that's being made by reading the document for ourselves. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, I just wanted to note that we don't have to read everything. Could you just explain here, in the middle it says that care should be taken that the military conscripts in -- with wartime assignments in units of the VJ, VTO, MUP, units of the SMO should not be on the lists of the population that is to be issued with weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, naturally. This is because the organ in charge of arming and equipping military conscripts and members of the units of the Army of Yugoslavia and MUP were -- that was another organ, and here we're talking about the Federal Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Let us move on. What were the relations of the Pristina Corps, or rather, at the beginning of 1999 in Kosovo and Metohija and during the state of war, did the state organs function; and if yes, which ones?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I personally know, even in this terrible chaos of war, all the state organs and all the local self government organs in Kosovo and Metohija functioned in accordance, as far as it was possible, and these local self government organs existed in the 29 municipalities, the organs of the Republic of Serbia operated in five districts, the Temporary Executive Council of the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija. I know that in the whole territory the public services functioned, health service, education, financial organs, judicial organs, everything that the civilian government comprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What were relations between the Pristina Corps and other agencies involved in defence, or rather, with the organs that you just enumerated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was cooperation whenever it was objectively possible to have this kind of cooperation, and primarily the purpose was to maintain the overall security system in the province, and in particular to provide assistance to those organs in taking care of all of the civilians in the chaos of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, what was the situation with the manning levels in the Pristina Corps at the beginning of the war in late March and early April when NATO air-strikes continued for two weeks already? So what were the manning levels in Pristina Corps at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the state of war was declared on the 24th of March, 1999, the Pristina Corps, in accordance with the plans, the mobilisation plan, was supposed to reach the wartime organization and strength of about 35.000 people within 72 hours. On the 24th of March, the corps had about 14.000 personnel, including the March intake of soldiers who had been retained in the ranks from the 15th of March onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us now look at a Prosecution exhibit, that's P1929, it's a report on the manning levels to the 3rd Army command. The date is the 31st of March. You told us what the situation was like on the 24th of March when the aggression started, but let us look at page 2 of this document. Could you please look -- well, we can't really tell the paragraphs apart. It's in the upper half of the page, it begins with the words "the Pristina Corps." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please read it and just comment on it in a couple of sentences because we have some figures here just so we know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At day plus seven," that's the eighth day of the war, "the Pristina Corps had 933 officers, that was 37 per cent; non-commissioned officers, 919, that was 48 per cent; soldiers 16.120, which was 54 per cent; a total number of 17.971, which was 52 per cent of the wartime establishment of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General. Thank you very much. Please tell us, by the 8th of April, 1999, that was the 14th day of the war, did all the units in the 3rd Army in Kosovo and Metohija, were they all resubordinated?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 7th of April, 1999, in Kosovo and Metohija there were the following units of the 3rd Army: The Pristina Corps, the Pristina Military District, and 202nd Logistics Base. On that day, the 3rd Army commander decided that the military district, the Pristina Military District and the 202nd would be resubordinated to the Pristina Corps until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at Exhibit 5D180.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said the order of the 3rd Army commander. It appears that you implemented this order, and it appears that it says so in this document. Could you please confirm that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my order, order from the Pristina Corps command, on the resubordination of these two units and the 3rd Army pursuant to the order of the 3rd Army commander dated the -- the date is the 8th of April, 1999, so that's the next day. This also regulates the procedure for the reporting, getting acquainted with the documents and tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you gave us a figure of just under 18.000 as the number of troops in the Pristina Corps eight days into the war. Did that number increase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me briefly reply to your question by giving you some information. Yes, it increased at a pace as much as it was possible through a selective and partial mobilisation in such a way that on D plus 15, that was the 15th day of the war, the strength was up to 21.000 troops, and on the 52nd day of the war, that was around the 15th of May, the corps reached its wartime manning level envisaged by the wartime organization and establishment, that figure was about 35.000 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What went wrong to prevent you doing it in the 72 hours you were supposed to do it in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what had been achieved by that time was, in fact, mission impossible, I say that as a soldier, because there were intensive air-strikes and intensive rebel activity throughout Kosovo and Metohija. So it was impossible to bring in troops in larger groups or unit per unit. We had to do it in smaller groups, selectively, and assessments had to be made to avoid casualties that could be inflicted both by the rebel forces and by NATO air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, you replied to His Honour Judge Bonomy's question, and thereby you pre-empted some of my questions. I would just like to ask you something more. The defence plans, the previous defence plans, did they envisage, apart from the manning levels bringing them up to strength, that there should be some additional vehicles brought in to bring them up to strength?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mobilisation plans regulated the recruitment and replenishment with materiel and equipment. You're now asking me about vehicles. When we're talking about the replenishment for the corps from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija the plans envisaged that around 530 motor vehicles should be mobilised in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija for the needs of the Pristina Corps. The replenishment was carried out up to the level of maybe 50 to 52 per cent, about 260 vehicles, and the overall replenishment of the vehicles from outside of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija was around 5.000 vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we will have a witness who will describe this in greater detail --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that an accurate figure in line 4 of page 7, 5.000?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I wasn't following the transcript, but this figure is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should it be 500?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, yes, from outside of Kosovo, Your Honours. For the replenishment from Kosovo, that's the lower figure, 530; and the overall replenishment from the overall territory of the FRY was 5.000 vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did I paraphrase you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, you told us that it was not until the 15th of May that the strength envisaged in the wartime formation was achieved. Were there any attempts to lessen the strength of PRK, to reduce the numbers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of April, 1999, the Pristina Corps command received an order from the 3rd Army command that in the following days selective disengagement of elements of the Pristina Corps should begin as part of the overall efforts of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to reduce the intensity of combat operations in Kosovo and Metohija and to contribute to the end of the war. And if the Trial Chamber allows me, just one more sentence. As far as I can remember, on the 13th of May I personally, as the corps commander in the sector of the village of Livadice in Podujevo, I saw off the first contingent, several buses full of military conscripts, who left the area of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, the transcript states that on the 9th of April, 1999, you received a 3rd Army order.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the 9th of May, but I might have misspoken. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, what happened immediately after your having brought the decision on the disengagement of part of the forces?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this decision was taken by the state leadership, and the corps command was executing the tasks of the 3rd Army command and the General Staff. I remember that there were quite a few journalists present who were following the corps' units, and that this also elicited diplomatic attention. Regrettably, I don't know about the further course of events in the diplomatic and political plain, but on the ground air-strikes and long-range NATO forces strikes escalated, as did the activities of the rebels, the strongest up to that point, and that happened as of the 12th and 13th of May, and on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at Exhibit 5D410, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this appears to be a document that is yours that you signed on the 12th of May, 1999. It states that it's very urgent and it is addressed to the commander personally. Can we have a brief comment from you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally drafted this order and I signed it, and that can be seen from the initials on it. And I sent an urgent order to the subordinated commanders personally because we had received information that NATO was preparing a second ground attack along a different axis, apart from the one that had been in course which was along the Kosare and Morina axis. And I ordered that every measure be taken to defend the routes and the -- persistently defend the state border and the integrity of the country throughout the defence area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in the second paragraph, please tell me whether I rightly take it that in addition to the part between the Kosare and Morina border posts where there was an attempt lasting several weeks to penetrate deep into the corps' zone, does that mean that there had been a successful attempt to penetrate before that or was this just -- am I concluding this rightly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your interpretation is correct because the aggressor's forces from the area of Albania were in the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at a depth between 500 and 1500 metres, holding salient features and endangering the complete axis towards Djakovica and Junik and threatening to compromise the entire defence of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we now take a look at Exhibit 5D411. This appears to be a corps command report on the very next day, the 13th of May, 1999, to the Supreme Command Staff. So please comment on the first and third paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I would call a special and alarming report. It is not a regular report. It was addressed to the Supreme Command Staff. The heading reads: "Pristina Corps command." This document was signed by the commander of the 3rd Army, who was at the corps command post because of the address and used its log informing the Chief of the General Staff of massive air-strikes on the 12th and 13th in the corps' area, over 230 missiles. And all the other paragraphs also inform on the fact that we do not have adequate forces to respond to counter such massive air-strikes and that the VJ -- the Pristina Corps units were threatened with massive casualties. And he requests and asks the General Staff for reinforcements in the system of anti-aircraft defence which I remember very well was soon forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And at page 2 you said amid this case of war, they used the Pristina Corps May log, and this was signed by the army commander who then sent his report to the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the commander, General -- Colonel-General Pavkovic, it is the seal and the memorandum of the corps because we were at one place. Someone could see this is a technical error amid the case of war, but the essence is as I have described.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, take a look at Exhibit P1495. This is a document of the Supreme Command Staff to the command of the 3rd Army. Can we have your comment on just item 1 and then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following these reports from the corps command and from the command of the 3rd Army, the General Staff dispatched a document in which -- in the first item of which it is stated that a statement had been prepared on the temporary postponement of the further implementation of the supreme commander's decision on the disengagement of the Yugoslav Army and MUP from Kosovo and Metohija because air-strikes as well as ground attacks had escalated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let us now move on to the admission of volunteers. How was the admission of volunteers to Pristina Corps units organized and regulated and how were they assigned to the units?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to man the Pristina Corps units with volunteers, two reception centres had been organized, had been set up, one within the 1st Army which was in Bubanj Potok, i.e., in Grocka, and the other one at the major military proving ground of the 2nd Army. The volunteers would pass through these two reception centres, and following the prescribed procedure, psychological, mental -- medical check-ups, et cetera, as well as additional combat training; and having completed all that, they would be assigned to the Pristina Corps units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, there is a mistake in the transcript. The 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Army, but we shall address that in a minute. Let us look at document 5D284, and please just explain a sentence -- one sentence in that document for me. You mentioned the centre in Medja where is this for the benefit of the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proving grounds, the automated proving grounds of major is military proving ground, which is some 30 kilometres away from Nis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It is not in the area of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is much farther from Kosovo and Metohija. It is farther than these 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We have the document before us now, General. We can read the rest of it for ourselves, but just tell me about item 1 which states: "Organize the admission, reception, and assignment of volunteers which are to be done in the reception or admissions centre of the 3rd Army ..." What does "organize the admission, reception, and assignment of volunteers ..." Actually stand for? What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command submitted to the command of the 3rd Army proposals, requirements, requests for the manning of certain specific units with volunteers. Following completed training and procedure in the 3rd Army admission centre, volunteers would be taken to the different war units along the corresponding routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we take a look, General, at Exhibit 5D338 at this point. This also is, it seems, one of your orders, and I should like to ask you to comment for us item 3.4 and explain for us the acronym, the abbreviation which features in it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my order of the 27th of March, regarding the admission, reception, and assignment of volunteers to war units. And in item 3 it is stated that volunteers should be assigned to lower-level units, lower-level units means lower-level units within brigades to battalions, that is according to their military occupational specialities, skill digits that they have been trained for.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will counsel please not overlap with the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In item 4 when -- you explained lower-level units are units which are lower than battalion or brigade or did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The designation, the name, for brigades in these conditions when we talk about manning war units and lower units are battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Fine. And who does the assigning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, you will need to leave a pause between answer and question, please. Please continue, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, you have explained. Who does the assigning of the volunteers to the brigades?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The volunteers for the brigade come from the admission or reception centre, and within the brigades, the brigade then assigns them within -- across its lower units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In item 4.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 4 states that at the level of the basic units which are companies, there are set up commissions that shall admit these people and provide additional equipment for them if this equipment is inadequate, acquaint them with the composition and their role of assignment within this basic unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you issue an additional order to the effect that volunteers could not be admitted to Kosovo and Metohija without verification, without checking at the admission centres? What measures did you take along those lines?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not order to the admission centres at the level of the army what they were to do, but irrespective of that procedure, which we of course were familiar with and which was observed, at the level of the corps additional measures were taken so that volunteers having been admitted, we would take additional security, psychological, medical processing, so to speak, as well as check their training level and their ability to use the resources, the weaponry, that we were armed with and equipped with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at 5D197.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, do you recognise this document, which again appears to be your own? This is an order of the 16th of April, 1999. Could you please comment on item 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it. There had been several orders in connection with this particular subject matter issued by the army command and the General Staff, the objective being to eliminate any observed shortcomings. And item 1 shows that it was ordered that at the level of the Pristina Military District there should be set up an admission subcentre as yet another institution that would help vet and assign volunteers to the corps war units on the one hand, and on the other hand if there should appear volunteers from the area of Kosovo and Metohija, they could not be received into the corps war units, but the subcentre of the Pristina Military District would send them every three days to the 3rd Army admission centre in the Medja area for them to go through the complete prescribed procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We'd like to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to what you have been saying now, it is paragraph 6 but on the second page, the one-but-last sentence before paragraph 7 starts. Could you please just read that sentence out for us, and is that what you were telling us about?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Taking volunteers --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, General, page 2. We can read that. Could you just read about checking volunteers. Is that what you told us?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every volunteer should be checked by a way of a question as to whether he wants to be trained at the Nis reception centre; if not, this person should not be taken in as a volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Tell us, do you know how many volunteers were taken in within the Pristina Corps; and if there were volunteers that were dismissed, how many of them were there and why?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the wartime units of the Pristina Corps, throughout the war a little over 1.400 volunteers were taken in. Through vetting and through decisions of wartime units in the corps command, almost one-third of these volunteers were dismissed on the following grounds. First of all, there were volunteers who could not take the war effort. They asked to be dismissed from wartime units, and it is on that basis, on those grounds, that some of them were dismissed. Secondly, there were volunteers who fell ill. They were sent to a military medical commission and were dismissed from wartime units. Thirdly, there were volunteers who did not observe the regimen of military discipline and the Rules of Conduct in Wartime, who were then dismissed from wartime units in handcuffs, arrested, and they were handed over to investigative military organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us try to illustrate this quickly what you've been telling us about. P -- 5D1938 -- P, P is what I'm asking for. P1938. I'd like to see page 2, please. Page 2, please. I have a version that's a bit better than this one. Could you please have a look at this where it says "pozitivno" -- no, rather, "negativno," which is at the very top of the page, it says: "On the 1st of April. Could you just give us your comment on that first statement, "on the 1st of April ..."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My command is as follows: The command of the 3rd Army informed the General Staff that on the 1st of April only a few days later, 25 volunteers were returned from the corps and seven were detained because of renegade behaviour, killings, robbery, rapes, et cetera, insubordination, and desertion also, among them there were two deaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we please have a look at Exhibit 5D215. Please take a look at 2.1, the last sentence just before 2.2. Could you read it out for us, it's short, and could you give us your comments.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the course of the morning, a group of volunteers, about 150 of them, were sent partly by -- on buses and partly by rail in an organized manner to Nis after their engagement in Metohija. This is my comment. The date is the 18th of April. This group of volunteers had taken part in heavy fighting in defending the state border at the Kosare-Morina section. They were under great stress. They requested to be disengaged, and we did that. I do apologise to the Trial Chamber not to be able to tell them more about this because our time is short. It's quite a story. It's a story that's quite long, because poisons were also used that destabilized many of the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Among that group of volunteers I see in one day there were 150 of them. Did this involve those who did not behave in accordance with military discipline?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. These were people who were at the border itself. Those who did not observe discipline had to be held accountable and could be disengaged only after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, the transcript does not correctly reflect what you said. The word used there is "poison," but I understood that you said "bojni otroui" chemical agents?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but I don't think we have time to discuss that. I know what this is about, specifically. Well, the number of 150 pertains to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us bring this story about the volunteers to an end. Could you please look at 5D392 and give us your comments briefly as to what this is about. It seems that there were attempts here to take a volunteer in without having been vetted first, and I think that you opposed that. I'm just trying to be of assistance so that we deal with the document quicker. Could you just read this sentence to us so that we could move on faster. So without reading it, could you just give us your comments and tell us what this is about, just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what this is about. From the command of the 3rd Army, or rather, from the Chief of Staff of the 3rd Army, a document came that had to do with something that was sent by the parents of a volunteer who came from the area around Belgrade. This was a complaint lodged by the parents. The mother complained to the command of the 3rd Army as to why we did not allow her son to go on being a volunteer. This is a volunteer who is the son of a military man, a lieutenant-colonel in the command of the Pristina Military District. I checked this through the commander of the Pristina Military District, whether he acted properly. He dismissed him because he did not go through the prescribed procedure, through army reception centres. And in this document I provide my reply, that the command of the military district noted this omission and that they acted properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was the Pristina Corps manned with non-Serbs from Kosovo and Metohija as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I shall try to be as accurate as possible now. There were over 1.000 military conscripts, non-Albanian in terms of their ethnic background, within the corps, Turks, Gorani, Romani.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were there attempts made to engage Albanians as well, to involve Albanians, ethnic Albanians, as they are called?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had occasion to familiarise ourselves with the order of the Chief of General Staff on the establishment of the 9th Detachment in Pristina that would consist of Albanians, including officers, officers and soldiers. Work was done in that direction. The military district commander testified to that. I issued a command but we did not succeed because they did not dare respond to the call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us look at this order; 5D183 is the number. 3.1 and 3.2 are the paragraphs I would like you to have a look at. Is that what you testified about? Is this your order? So far we've had a problem without having the English translation, and now we have for the first time the problem of not having the Serbian translation. It's a good thing that we have that problem for once as well.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, this is my order that is in line with the order issued by the army commander and the Chief of General Staff on the establishment of the 9th Military Territorial Detachment in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let's move on faster. We can all read it. We can all read and realise that what you said is there. Were there any requests by citizens who were ethnic Muslims who were not military conscripts to get involved in the Army of Yugoslavia, to join the ranks of the Army of Yugoslavia? I would like to see 5D370. In the meantime you can give me an answer.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, about ten days after this unsuccessful attempt in Pristina, I got a request and a proposal from the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade to have a large number of citizens of Muslim and Gorani ethnicity who were asking to be involved in the defence of the integrity of the country. We can see the document here right in front of us, of the command of the Pristina Corps. I am making a proposal to the command of the 3rd Army on the basis of the request made by the brigade to establish a detachment consisting of 200 men in Sredacka Zupa, according to a particular establishment, and in order to have specific tasks carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We are going to move on. I would just like to direct the Trial Chamber to the following. Yesterday we talked about uniforms that military conscripts had kept and that were used. Let us not go back to that now. The references are 5D -- Exhibit 5D188 and 184. From the documents we can see what it was that you testified about, so let us move on. General, did you insist --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a mistake in the -- mistake. 5D187 and 5D184 are the numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you take any measures in terms of the personal appearance of the members of the corps?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't take -- I wouldn't say any measures or some measures. With the permission of the Trial Chamber, in this war chaos the corps command and the subordinate units really and truly took many measures in terms of disciplined conduct on the part of unit members, including personal appearance, behaviour, wearing uniforms, using weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we are going to get to that specifically. Could you please look at 5D898, it's a Defence exhibit. This is an order of the commander of the 549th Motorised Brigade dated the 30th of April, 1999, that is based on your order of the 29th of April, 1999. In paragraph 3 -- well, actually, can you read it out to us and can you give us your comments?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Insist relentlessly on the proper personal appearance of all members of the brigade and on the protection of the reputation of the Army of Yugoslavia at any cost." This has been copied from the order issued by my corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us look at your order of the 7th of May, that's 5D398. It seems that here, too, the measure about the conduct of the members of the corps outside of the zone -- could you comment on item 1.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order I demand at all levels of command that information should be obtained about the movements of the members of the units in uniform and with weapons outside of the combat zone, and once again, I prohibit any movement of military personnel with weapons outside of the sector of their own unit, except if they are there to carry out some kind of an official task. And I make responsible for the consistent implementation of this order the commanders, and they are to provide me with regular reports about that. They are to report on that in combat reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let us go back to -- we've seen what the basic tasks of the Pristina Corps were in combat operations and in the tasks in the organization of the defence, that's 5D366, that's the exhibit number. I would like to ask for it. This is about issuing tasks in the organization of the defence, and I am -- would be interested to hear your comments on item 7. Could you please read it and comment on it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ensure full compliance with the security regime in the territory, with focus on protecting the units, the public order, preventing crime, and protecting civilians. Complete the full clear-up of the terrain." This order followed on the same day, the 5th of April, when the commanders subordinate to the 3rd Army commander submitted their reports on the preparations for the drafting of a new defence plan in the area of the 3rd Army and the Pristina Corps in accordance with the Grom 4 plan. I didn't wait for the order from the army commander to come, but as soon as this meeting was completed I issued an order, I issued relevant orders, and among them was this task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we spoke about -- we saw evidence from May indicating that the -- the penetration of the ground forces between Morina-Kosare, those border posts continued. When did this incursion actually begin, on what date?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to say that the federal government declared a unilateral cessation of hostilities on the 6th of April, and on one of the greatest religious feasts in the Orthodox religion, the 9th of April, that's Easter, the Orthodox Easter, there was a ground aggression launched by a very strong force from Albania along the Kosare and Morina axis and on to Pristina -- on to Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To confirm what you just said, could you please look at item 2 in this document, and did you, in fact, order the cease-fire pursuant to the decision of the federal government?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. "On the 6th of April, at 2000 hours, stop all active operations of the corps apart from a direct attack on our units," but this was the decision of the federal government.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 5D185.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, it appears to be a report from the 3rd Army commander to the chief of Supreme Command Staff and the date is the 11th of April. Could you please briefly comment on this. Is this what you were telling us about, and we can see that there is an estimate of the enemy strength.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document from the 3rd Army command dated on the 11th, but on the 10th he sent another telegram with a similar content. And as you can see, I initialled this telegram, approving that it may be sent because the army commander had already left in accordance with his own plans. And we informed the chief of the Supreme Command Staff that ground attacks from Albania continue, and a proposal is made to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to take diplomatic measures to inform the United Nations and the world public through diplomatic channels about this ground aggression that is launched against the territory of Yugoslavia from Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me just a minute. Your Honour, there's a very serious problem with this translation. It doesn't tell us what this document really is. It says it's to the 3rd Army command and actually it's from the 3rd Army command, that language doesn't appear in the B/C/S. It goes to the Supreme Command Staff and the translation says it's going to the Pristina Military District command. That language doesn't appear in the B/C/S. So it's a completely wrong translation at least of the heading part of that document and very misleading in that regard. It needs to be replaced with a proper translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The direction of the document is clarified in the transcript I think. Is that correct, it's from the 3rd Army command and it's to the Supreme Command Staff. And therefore, to that extent, the position is accurately reflected in the transcript and what you're suggesting is the document itself should be submitted for retranslation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It has to be, Your Honour, because I have visions of a Prosecutor standing up and arguing on appeal that the English translation is correct, that's happened to me before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You must have difficulties sleeping, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So I really think it has to be -- I think that the transcript doesn't solve the problem. I think the document has to be fixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remind me of the number of this document, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bakrac, it's for you to resubmit this to be -- for the translation to be revised and then to make a filing to substitute the revised version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us look at 5D195. I hope we'll have more luck with the translation. Could you please look at this document carefully. Later on we will -- and there has been quite some evidence from the Prosecution witnesses regarding an action that took place a few days after this order of yours, but of course this order does not refer to that. But in order to be able to understand that later on, could you please comment on this document. It's dated the 15th of April, 1999, the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally drafted this document. Having assessed the dramatic situation that was the result of the penetration of the state border and the violation of the sovereignty of the country, I made the decision that in a non-military parlance the most special elements within the corps for the struggle against the terrorist foreign mercenaries and specials should take part in protecting the integrity of the state by forming a special detachment from the Pristina Corps command containing elements from the 72nd Special Brigade that had been resubordinated to us from the military police battalion, the corps military police; and to dispatch them as soon as possible to Djakovica sector, where they would be received by the Chief of Staff of the corps. They would place themselves under his control and they would be engaged in defending the integrity of the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the Karaula --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosare-Morina axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Which is adjacent to which river valley?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This axis leads directly to the Caragoj valley, to Junik and Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell us, and we will be able to proceed more quickly, how long did this ground operation last, the invasion along this axis?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This operation which quite well-known to military analysts, both domestic, Serbian, and Yugoslav, and foreign military analysts, is known as Strela 1. It lasted until the end of the war, but they were not able to penetrate any deeper than they had right at the beginning of the aggression.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, if I'm not mistaken, you issued a special order for the routing and destruction in the border belt in the broader area of -- in the broader sector of Kosare; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me, this order has four pages, we'll be analysing it later on, there's no need to open it or analyse it now. Could you tell us how you designate the command structures, who was to be in command of this operation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since this was a special task of operational significance, although the forces engaged were quite small, I ordered that the Chief of Staff of the corps should be in direct command of this task force.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From where?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Djakovica sector, and further on towards the border itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From the Djakovica forward command post?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the forward command post in the wider Djakovica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we have to make pauses. I am more to blame than you are here, but we both have to try and make the interpreters' job easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is a mistake in the transcript. The date was not recorded, that's the order of the 8th of May, 1999, and that's 5D401.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, was there a ground operation or a ground incursion in any other part of the state border?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By Your Honours' leave I would like to say just one sentence. Throughout this time NATO applied its doctrine of air-ground battle. This is one specific operation, it's a ground operation, along a single axis, and then after 45 days there was another ground operation in the Vrbnik axis, that's the Gorozub border post, the Pastrik mountains, in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at 5D231.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Again this may be a translation issue. I have to say I don't understand what's just been said by the witness. He said: "I would like to say just one sentence. Throughout this time NATO applied its doctrine of air-ground battle. This is one specific operation, it's a ground operation, along a single axis ..." Now, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please clarify. You heard what His Honour said. Could you just briefly clarify this misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to say that throughout the war there was this operation underway, aggression against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, from air and on the ground. In NATO doctrine, this is called air-ground battle, and we are talking specifically about two ground operations. The first started on the 9th of April and extended until the end of the war on an axis leading towards Djakovica; and the other one happened on the 26th of May and lasted until the 13th of June, when the agreement had already been signed, that was in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your answer earlier gave the impression that the ground operation started at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 9th of April was the penetration; that is what I call the ground aggression, not counting the lesser-scale attacks at the very outset of the war and the incursions in that period into the Kosovo and Metohija territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment until I go back a little. Please continue, Mr. Bakrac. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, the combat report describes this.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now call 5D231.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is a combat report of the corps command to the 3rd Army. This is perhaps not in constance with our current topic, but look at this. On the 26th and the 27th, NATO aviation continued to shell the region of Djakovica with over 10 missiles. Are you aware of this bombing of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday when I was explaining the isolation of the battle-field by NATO aerial bombing, it can be seen in this report. When there are land operations across the border, there is aerial bombing by NATO forces in depth of the territory in order to prevent the bringing in of forces to actually stabilize the defence on the axis of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you look at item 2 and then we will continue. Is that the second land operation that you were referring to, item 1.2? Immediately on the next page it is item 1.2 and it begins with the words "with strong ..."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was already the second day of the land operation called Strela 2 on this axis in which participated also the artillery units of the armed forces of Albania, not only the terrorist forces gathered from the wide areas of Europe and all over the place, and with exceptionally intensive bombing by NATO air force with over 211 impact -- high-impact missiles. This will remain remembered in the analysis of warfare. B-52s actually shelled targets of company rank on this axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us look at another combat report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 5D234 -- actually, it is dated the 1st of June, the 1st of June, 1999, 5D234.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is also a combat report to the command of the 3rd Army by the corps command, and under item 1.1, last paragraph; and under item 1.2, first paragraph, that is what I would like you to comment on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1.1, activities of the NATO armed forces. The NATO air forces continued conducting intensive reconnaissance over flights and attacks in the corps zone, and specifically in item 1.2, "in the course of 31st of May, enemy aviation shelled, bombed incessantly for 12 hours, including B-52 bomber aircraft, the positions of the 1st Battalion of the 549th Motorised Brigade, firing over 200 missiles, with a simultaneous land assault, land attack, from the Republic of Albania along the Gorozup axis with several hundred enemy soldiers." Let me add, I was personally on that particular axis with the army commander on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We shall now move on. Before we proceed, how many defensive battles were there and what were the casualties the Pristina Corps sustained during that period and how was this reflected on the security status on the zone of the border?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As part of the defensive operation of the corps, on 250-kilometre front and 100- to 120-kilometres in-depth, there were several hundred battles and clashes, but the focus of the defensive operation was in the front area facing Albania and in the first defensive echelon. There were casualties, 280 soldiers were killed, 760 were wounded -- actually, counting for 52 per cent of all the war losses, war casualties at the Pristina Corps level.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, how many battles and combat engagements were there, approximately, for us -- in order for us to paint a picture, because you did say that but it is not recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said several hundred. In the combat reports of the corps, 552 battles and combat engagements are registered, but I'm quite sure that not all of them were registered because there were daily attacks by the armed rebels in various locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We saw that the Ministry of the Interior was supported in executing the counter-terrorist activities on the basis of previous plans and special orders of the kind of Grom 3. What was the objective of taking such counter-terrorist activities, i.e., supporting them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these combat activities were component part of the defensive operation of the corps. As regards specific counter-insurgency actions of the army forces and of the MUP forces, their general objective was to lift the blockade on the main roads and important facilities, important features, to lift the blockade on them by the armed rebels, also to prevent own units -- to protect own units, to protect the general population, and to establish as secure a regime of life and work as possible a war security regime in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. That was the overall objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see Prosecution Exhibit P2447.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is a Prosecution exhibit and deployment chart of the KLA in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Could you comment on these zones in conjunction with this previous question, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a layout, the overview map that we had seen when the witness Zyrapi was testifying, and it originates in the leadership or the headquarters, the Main Staff, of the KLA, as was explained to us at that time. And then these shaded areas, I recognise the most important concentrations of the armed rebel's forces throughout Kosovo and Metohija and in the border area facing Albania and Macedonia as well as in central Kosovo and Metohija and in the north of the province.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When did the command of the 3rd Army issue its executive order for taking possession of the defensive sector and anti-terrorist struggle?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember at this point, on the day when the imminent threat of war was declared on the 23rd of March, 1999, the command of the army issued an executive order for taking possession of positions to defend the country and begin the defence of the country's integrity and sovereignty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is Defence Exhibit 5D1294. There is no need for us to call it up to appear on the screen. General, in keeping with these orders and plans, when did the counter-terrorist activities of a part of the corps units begin? You talked about this yesterday. Just tell us when and did the command of the corps request a report from the units after the execution of such actions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order which we did not have occasion to see, I remember that in one item the army commander ordered that with the start of the NATO aggression there should be -- the defensive positions should be manned, should be possessed, and counter-insurgency activities initiated with the objective of protecting the units and enabling the operational deployment of the corps' units. So the answer is the first counter-insurgency activities were on the 24th of March and continued from then on. And to respond to your second question, unless I have omitted something, is that the corps command regularly, periodically, required of the subordinated commands interim, special, reports besides the daily, regular, ones, in which the brigades were to provide a brief analysis of the implementation of their previous tasks in defending the country.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we take a look at Exhibit 5D343 and can we have your comment on it. This appears to be your document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a document of the corps command which I, myself, drafted on the 29th of March, following the successfully executed action of routing terrorist forces in the area of Drenica. It required the corps command be submitted data on the realisation of that task, in particular requiring an analysis of the training levels of the units for such tasks of their combat skills of the units, that is in item 4. In item 5, the implementation of coordinated action with units of army and MUP. And in item 6, I require their information about treatment of civilians during combat activities and observance of the international law of war, and naturally, to inform me of any observed terrorist activities by the terrorist forces. And I'm asking them to send me written reports by the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Take a look at 5D339 of the 28th of March now. Tell me what this document is and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to ask the Trial Chamber for its indulgence. I would like to remind you of my previous answer when we were discussing some orders that bore that strange title, the Joint Command, where I testified that the units were directed in a number of documents to those tasks. And this is now a preparatory order that I issued to the units after the counter-insurgency action in Drenica and the preparation for a new action to take place in the Malisevo area, where each unit is given a specific task within this order for preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did the 3rd Army command report to the Supreme Command Staff about those actions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The 3rd Army command monitored the implementation of these tasks, it approved, and definitely it reported to its superior command, which would be the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you now look at P1446 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do that, why do you relate this to the Joint Command issue, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, two actions are mentioned here, one is Drenica, the other one is Malisevo. For both these actions orders that bear no signature were issued, ones that are headed "Joint Command for KiM." And yesterday, I tried to explain what it meant, the fact that this was sent to the units, but there were other documents that made it clear to them who was actually ordering this and what was actually being ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, I remember that. And what's this got to do with the format of these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, because after the 28th of March, the commanders would again receive the order for Malisevo where there would be the heading of "the Joint Command for KiM," which means what I actually tried to explain yesterday. But before that, they had already been given a specific task from the corps commander with the signature, and they know what they are to do. They will face no dilemma once they receive the order that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying that there would be a preparatory order which says nothing about Joint Command and then an executive order which mentions the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a good example of a preparatory order where there's no mention at all of the Joint Command. This is the Pristina Corps, and there will be a group of documents that would follow this one, including the order that is unsigned with the heading of the Joint Command in order to indicate that this task was to be carried out with the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you have no further questions on this topic, I have a couple of questions on this topic, but we are now approaching --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, continue with other couple of questions, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, on, or rather, my previous question was: Did the 3rd Army command report to the Supreme Command Staff on these actions? And could you please look at Prosecution Exhibit P1446. Could you please comment on it. This is a very brief document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 3rd Army from the forward command post, which is at the corps command post, on the 30th of March informs the Supreme Command Staff that on the 30th of March an operation will commence to destroy the remaining terrorist forces in the Malisevo area. And in accordance with his estimate, the action would be completed within the next two or three days. This is the action that is mentioned in the previous preparatory order, and this is the action to which one of those documents with the heading of the Joint Command would pertain to.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please look at Exhibit P2029 and could you please comment on this document, in particular regarding items 2 and 4.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the corps command from the beginning of the war. It is a preparatory order for the next action, as was the previous order, where I order that the Malisevo operation - although it was not really an operation - should be completed by the 1st of April, in accordance with the previous plan. And then that the forces should be regrouped for further tasks; in other words, what I'm trying to say is that the corps command is monitoring the situation, controlling the situation, commanding the units, taking appropriate measures. It is in command of its own units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please comment on item 4, it's on the next page, together with this order to control and block the Jablanica area, could you please look at paragraph -- item 4 and tell us what you meant by it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, Your Honour. Could I inquire when we're breaking today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As soon as we finish this document, Mr. -- I don't believe in interrupting at an unnatural moment if it's possible to avoid it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wasn't clear because of the unusual sitting hours today starting at 11.00 and we typically don't go more than an hour and 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. We're almost finished this, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do apologise, I didn't want to interrupt --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just deal with this and complete the document rather than go back to it later, which is a real waste of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Paragraph 4, item 4.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although this is a classical example of a combat order, in this order too, in item 4, I insist that in all the garrisons, in all the deployment areas in coordinated action with forces of the MUP, the military territorial organs, the military prosecutor's offices, and military investigating and judicial organs, I know what this is all about, despite the fact that now the text is no longer on the screen. Do I have to talk about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, please, just tell us about it. Don't read it.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I demand that a stable security regime be established, that the civilian population be protected in direct coordination with all these structures, that crimes of all sorts are to be prevented. And I also demand that special forces and people should be set aside for this task, primarily from the military police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I have two more questions and two brief documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, not any more documents at this stage, Mr. Bakrac. Let's be reasonable about it, and indeed this is just a demonstration of something that is quite unnecessary, because all the witness has done is tell us what we can read for ourselves on the screen. I thought I was assisting in allowing you to complete this, but it really hasn't assisted very much. We'll break now and resume at ten minutes to 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.51 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, prior to the break we were looking at this document. To clarify matters can we have Exhibit P2003 of the Prosecution shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is one of the orders tendered by the Prosecution. The date is the 2nd of April, 1999, and it is an order to smash and destroy the STS in the Jablanica sector. The heading states "Joint Command." Can we now have Exhibit 5D84 shown on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is a combat report of the Pristina Corps dated the 3rd of April. The previous command was of the 2nd of April, this is of the 3rd of April. General, please comment on item 2.1, activities, results, consequences, and other, and focus on the first sentence, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This combat report, it's item 2.1, the first sentence thereof states -- in it I actually inform the commander of the army that on the basis of my own decision, the decision of the Pristina Corps commander, the re-grouping of forces has been completed and that actions are in course to rout terrorist forces according to the Jablanica plan in the Jablanica sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just a minute and then we shall wrap it up. Let us -- we shall revert to this report later, but let us just take a look at Exhibit 5D85 one minute, which I believe is a combat report in the form of a telegram dated the next day, the 4th of April, 1999. Please read first sentence of item 2.1, activities, effects, consequences, and other data the next day, i.e., April 4th, 1999.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation, the action, aimed at crushing the terrorist forces in the wider Jablanica region is underway, and following the decision of the commander of the Pristina Corps shall be completed by nightfall of the 4th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell us now, General, did you on the 3rd of April, 1999, and on the 4th of April, 1999, when this indictment was not yet in existence, did you write in your report to the superior command what you explained to us today and yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is the substance and that reflects the factual state of affairs, the goings on in the zone of responsibility of the corps in the relevant period; namely, the corps command was planning to use -- was planning the use of units in the -- to defend the country and informed the superior command on that particular -- on the implementation of that particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us go back to 5D84 for a minute. I apologise, I omitted something, item 8. In order to establish a link with this document, I proceeded too quickly. So please tell us what is the focus of activities for the coming day, according to item 8. Yes, we have it on the screen now, item 8, that is.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I informed the army commander that the focus for the next day would be to continue the initiated action to rout terrorist forces in the Jablanica area. If I need to amplify --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, thank you, that will suffice.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have seen this document many times in regard to the explanation of when the 37th Motorised Brigade was resubordinated, and the number of criminal charges filed for criminal offences; all this has been dealt with and addressed in dealing with other witnesses. We shall now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, what is the particular point you're making by reference to 5D84 and 85 and P2003?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is evident here that then, on the 3rd April 1999, the corps commander at the time when there was no indictment, it does not refer to the -- to an order of the Joint Command but refers to an order of the Pristina Corps, as he told us yesterday. In the combat report, you first saw the Jablanica order which has in its heading "Joint Command." And the next day in the combat report, the corps commander says: "On the basis of the decision of the commander of the Pristina Corps ..." And does not say on the basis of the decision of the Joint Command. So on the 3rd and 4th of April, he refers to it as the decision of the commander of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought that was the case, it's just the reference to the indictment has defeated me, but let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to indicate for the record that 5D85 does not appear to have been on the notification list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Please continue, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that I've seen it with some of the colleagues but perhaps colleague Visnjic --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is probably with me and I do not object to its being used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we shall now move on. Did the staff of the Supreme Command issue orders and warnings for the protection of its own forces against KLA attacks?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall there were such orders which were invoked by the army command, and certainly when it was so assessed by the Supreme Command Staff it did issue such orders as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we take a look at 5D -- Exhibit 5D174. 5D174.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please give us a brief comment on items 2 and 3 so that we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that an order of the 3rd Army had a similar content, on the basis of which I issued my own order, and the essence is purely of a military doctrinal nature, namely, that prior to bringing to specific areas and facilities of units, such has to be carried out, combat control, and the insight must be gained into the area, whether it is secure to deploy the units there and protect them from any possible actions by terrorist forces. And in the third item, the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command orders the same to the army commander, namely, to act in compliance with the order. And I also received such an order and instructions to act upon it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did the forces of the Ministry of the Interior in conditions when the KLA insurgency and the NATO aggression began, were they able to execute such complete combat control and protect the men and the facilities?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even had there been many times their number, they would not have been able to complete that task on their own against the sitting of the armed rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we shall now take a look at another document, which I should like you to comment on in more detail. I believe that that is your document dated the 9th of April, 1999, which is exhibit -- Defence Exhibit 5D476. You see the document, General, can you explain to us your sentence "to the commanders," what is this about?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall this document because it was created at the time when the land aggression began from Albania on the Kosare-Djakovica axis. The operations organ of the Pristina Corps informed me that they had received information from organs of the MUP staff which were engaged in planning to the effect that secretariats of the interior in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija were planning or had planned specific counter-terrorist actions. And in that sense, I ordered the commanders to establish contact with the secretariats of the interior, to identify their place and role in terms of their potential to engage in coordinated action with the MUP forces, to implement the tasks of combat control of the territory. And in the heading I also warned the commanders that one of the priority tasks of the corps was incessant and complete control and securing of the territory. I stated that they should identify the concrete activities by secretariat, that they should identify their own potentials for coordinated activity, and then that they were to draft proposals.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, yes, let us not go into detail. You did indicate what factors were to be established, contact with for consultation and coordination. Let us look at page 2, item 4, the last two sentences, I should like to hear your comment on those, then we shall move on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I ordered that once contacts, coordination, have been established in accordance with the possibilities of the units, specific actions should be planned and that such plans should be submitted to the Pristina Corps command for its approval. Thus, what was planned by the MUP forces, the army units, the Pristina Corps as their actions, they were to act in coordination in carrying out their tasks wherever they could, and the plans would be approved by the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And did you ask that analyses be submitted to you of those actions? Please look at 5D373.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a document issued by the corps command, although in the letterhead the title of the corps command is missing and the date is the 23rd of April. And in this document I ask of the subordinate commanders that they send information on the action against the rebel forces in places where those participated in the action, and the names of the actions are listed if the forces participated in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let's move on. We have seen a number of documents of yours mentioning combat control of the territory. Can you explain to us the essence or the gist of the significance of this and the manner in which combat control of the territory was exercised.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With Their Honours' leave, I ask you to bear with me and allow me to respond in a few sentences, because this activity differed from the usual combat activities which we call combat actions, attack, or defence. Combat control of the territory is a set of different tactical combat activities with the aim of primarily through passive, defensive, intelligence, counter-intelligence, and other measures protecting the units and major facilities. The set of measures and activities varies. It ranges from taking up positions or taking facilities to setting up observation posts, setting up check-points, and by all these means combat control of the territories achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's look at Exhibit 5D374. General, we will come to your special orders relating to taking care of the civilian population, but we have seen that in your combat orders you also demanded that your units adhere by the law of war, international laws of war and humanitarian law. In these orders for the control of the territory, we also see that there is a special item dealing with that. Could you explain, first of all, in item 1 why did you require that all military territorial units be removed from inhabited places, and then please go on and comment on items 2 and 3. The date here is the 23rd of April.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the military and doctrinal standpoint, this order of mine - and there was also a previous order issued by the army commander - is not fully justified because military doctrine implies organizing defence by relying on inhabited places and fortified facilities and buildings. However, I ordered that military territorial units which by virtue of their purpose carry out their tasks in inhabited places, protecting crucial facilities be removed from inhabited places, and I did this for two reasons. Firstly, with Their Honours' leave I will simplify things by saying that we wanted to create a safe place where the civilian population would have room to live without hindrance, as far as is possible in wartime conditions. And on the other hand, we wanted them to take certain facilities outside inhabited places, that is, the units, we wanted the units to take up facilities outside inhabited places in order to achieve combat control.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
