utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We see at the end of this document that again you say that information about possible sectors for the reception of new temporarily displaced persons should be found.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the displaced people had gone back to their homes, particularly to Pristina, Podujevo, to the east [as interpreted], and in the preparatory part, I asked the brigade commanders to get in touch with the representatives of the civilian authorities and to provide them with all the assistance in providing accommodation of those displaced civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, page 90, line 19, it says "to the east," actually it's the place in Kosovo called the Istok which is -- in Serbian it's the same word, Istok is east, but in this case it was the name of the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you from your subordinate commands, we have seen these two documents, receive any feedback about those orders that you had issued?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In implementing these orders, all the brigades sent in reports on efforts to receive the refugees, the displaced persons, about the efforts to take them back to their homes, to take care of them, and about everything that the corps units had done in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can we look at 5D1101 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To see whether the commands subordinate to the brigades sent such orders out, 5D1101. This is the command of the 52nd Mechanised Artillery Brigade --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, mixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's dated the 22nd of April, 1999. It says here: "Pursuant to an order of the Pristina Corps command dated the 19th of April," so we will be opening those orders. They will be dated every other day, but you can see here there's a reference to the 19th of April. And it says here: "Relating to providing shelter for the refugees in -- and because of the continuing NATO air-strikes against the Yugoslav Army units and the expected ground invasion result in an increased movement of the civilian population in the units' area of responsibility which considerably aggravates the overall security situation," and it goes on like that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order is in line with the order from the Pristina Corps command that in contact with the Gnjilane MUP organs and the adjacent brigade, that the civilian population should be taken care of as much as possible, as was ordered by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at Exhibit 5D11 -- I'm sorry, 390.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is the command of the 2nd Artillery Rocket Brigade from Djakovica, that's the anti-aircraft artillery and rocket unit, and they provide you with the information as to where the accommodation for the civilian population had been found and they provide additional locations for such accommodation in the future.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They indicate the settlements where the civilian population is put up. They stated that on the 4th of May there were 35 to 40.000 people in Djakovica and that it was possible to accept a new group of displaced persons, that there were facilities to accept them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I selected documents that are relevant for various areas in Kosovo, so we have another exhibit which is related to Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters didn't catch the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The exhibit number, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D486.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us proceed quickly. It appears on the basis of this report dated the 4th of May you again receive information about locations where it is possible to receive civilian population, but it is interesting to note that we have the same problem of communication, the road communication for Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 354th Infantry Brigade had really a lot of work with the civilian authorities, finding shelter for the civilian population. There was also the medical battalion in the corps, and they joined in. 50.000 displaced persons who had come back from Macedonia were taken care of, but here he warns that on the Podujevo-Luzane axis there is a strong terrorist presence and they pose a threat to the civilian population. In light of the fact that I demanded that the military should physically secure the deployment sectors, he is trying to tell me that he doesn't have enough forces, enough troops, to carry all that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 5D793 is another exhibit that speaks to this, it is a report from the 7th PBR. And could we please have 5D1033 up on the screen. This is the command of the 37th Motorised Brigade, the date is the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you comment on it, because this follows immediately after your order of the 19th, the command of the 37th Motorised Brigade issues this order.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Acting pursuant to the order of the corps command, the commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade ordered his units to take the measures that I defined in the towns of Srbica and Glogovac, he demands from his subordinates to get in touch with the representatives of the authorities, the civilian protection, and the MUP, and to do that together. And they really, really evinced a great deal of concern and care for the civilian population in Drenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 5D1004 up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you also issue orders to the military district commands once they were resubordinated to you, to the effect that the civilian population should be protected and taken care of?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is just one military district command, not commands, because the other military district was the one in Nis that was subordinate to the army commander. But yes, here we see a very clear order from the military district commander to take care of the civilian population, to report on it, and to take all other measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could we now please look at Exhibit 5D1037, dated the 3rd of May, 1999. If you could explain to us what this is all about, and if we could see what you did when you get -- when you got the feedback about this problem from the commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade sent a number of such reports from the 3rd of May onwards to the corps command and personally to me, reporting to me that the civilian authorities in the town of Glogovac were not functioning, that the civilian population was at the brink of barely surviving, that there was not enough food, that there was great danger, that there would be outbreaks of disease, that there wasn't enough water. So he was asking for help basically to take care of the civilian population because he did not have the assets to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And what did you do after that, General?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from sending logistics organs from the corps there to verify whether the corps command organs could do something, I also wrote to the president of the Temporary Executive Council of Kosovo and Metohija, Mr. Andjelkovic, and I asked him in his capacity of the executive organ in the province to take measures to help the population in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us look at this exhibit, and I would like to ask you to read the last paragraph to see what you wanted the president of the Temporary Executive Council to do, that's Exhibit 5D412. It appears -- well, there is no medical care, water, and power in the town and food-supplies are running low. This is what you reported to the president of the Temporary Executive Council, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel and witness please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is correct. I informed the president of the Temporary Executive Council of the province of Kosovo and Metohija about the problems that the civilian population was facing, the problems about taking care of them in the centre of Drenica on the basis of the report that I had received from the brigade commander, notifying him that the brigade command and the MUP organs in the field actually tried to do something using their own assets and resources and that we were not in a position to assist them, that we were not able to do so. And I propose that at the level of the province government and the civilian protection structure, that this report be considered as a matter of urgency and that urgent measures be taken to feed the population and to provide medical care. As we have already heard from Mr. Andjelkovic, who has testified recently - and I know that for a fact - he did act upon this proposal or demand, if I should put it that way, and he sent Mr. Andric and some other people that he trusted and they provided assistance to this population, food and medicine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, I have to apologise to you, I'm a little bit tired. I asked you the wrong question when I said you sent the report. I actually meant to say you notified. But this is an example of the cooperation between the civilian authorities and the military where you were able to do so, when you were able to assist, you signalled this to the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the most important thing is that the fact that I talked to the president of the Temporary Executive Council, this actually helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have 5D506 of the 27th of April, 1999, which also describes measures to provide to the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we take a look at another two other documents, the first is 5D816, dated the 23rd of April. This is an order on the relocation on military territorial detachments from inhabited places. Please comment on item 3, it is not very long. Or read it out for us. I think that it is really important from the aspect of the things that you have been charged with.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have accentuated repeatedly -- I accentuated repeatedly and ordered that inhabited places should -- that military units should leave inhabited places in order to create, as I said today, living space for the return and normal life of the civilian population on the one hand; and on the other, if there were any units -- if -- if units were found possibly in that area, they would be the target of all terrorist and NATO forces, so that commander of the 7th Infantry Brigade in the area of the Istok and Klina towns in item 3 ordered his units to accelerate the return of civilians going back to their towns and villages which they had left. He also said that civilian shelters in the sectors of defensive units should not be allowed and that civilians should be ensured to return -- allowed -- enabled to return to the settlements which they had earlier abandoned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Another question on this topic: Did you act in concert and coordination with the MUP forces in order to provide for the civilian population? And while we wait for your answer can we have Exhibit 5D365 brought up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR LAZAREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should say that all these activities were undertaken in coordination and cooperation with the civilian authorities and with the MUP forces in the field. This order is one from the initial period of the war, one that I drafted personally. And in items 1 as well as 2 and the other ones, I insisted that in concert with the MUP forces of the Republic of Serbia the regime of security should be fully implemented, focusing not only on the protection of units and law and order, but also the protection of the civilian population. In the areas of combat activities, the work and engagement of military and judiciary investigative and judicial organs should be ensured, and all members of units should be called to account. And the next item states that a system should be rendered to MUP forces on protecting and ensuring the return of displaced persons. So all these measures were done in consultations and coordination in order for all of us together to assist the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave I should like to move on to a new topic. I do not need private session and I'm not -- I'm feeling rather poorly. So if I can ask you that we finish, that we adjourn, some ten minutes earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if that's the position, we shall, but you seem to me to be needing every minute that's available to you the way this is progressing. But if you feel that you can't make use of these ten minutes, we have to accept that from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I feel feverish, Your Honours. All of a sudden I have started to make mistakes in asking my questions, and I do not really feel capable of continuing. Were there more time, I would really do my utmost, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We shall adjourn until Monday. Mr. Lazarevic, this is a particularly important stage of your evidence. It's vital, as I've said before, that in the breaks between your periods on the witness-stand that you have no discussion whatsoever with any person about the evidence in this case, that's without exception. There's no person with whom you should have any discussion about the evidence. We'll adjourn now and we will resume on Monday here at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of November, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.22 p.m.,
